title: The Quiet Kennels
hook: I work nights at an animal shelter, and there's one rule: if the dogs ever go quiet all at once, don't walk the kennels.
lines: I work the overnight shift at an animal shelter, way out on a county road.
Forty dogs. And all night long... they never stop barking.
The woman who trained me gave me one rule.
If the dogs ever go quiet all at once... don't walk the kennels.
Stay in the office. Keep the light on. And wait for them to start again.
For two months, they barked till sunrise. Every single night.
Then, last night, just after three... all forty stopped. At the exact same second.
I sat at my desk... and listened to nothing.
Then, at the far end of the row, the last kennel gate creaked open.
Slow footsteps. Bare feet on wet concrete... coming toward the office.
I looked up at the security monitor... at the camera above my own desk.
Something tall was standing right behind my chair, holding one long finger to its lips.
The dogs hadn't gone quiet on their own... it had asked them to.
